contributes.instructions: Pasting HTML on the canvas (Cmd+V with markup as plain text, or text/html that is more than a single paragraph of prose; a paragraph copied from a page lands as canvas text through the Text plugin instead) lands it as one new daydream.viewport page, 960px wide and selected. The page is what was pasted, cleaned exactly as ingest cleans a page: whatever could run (script, embed, object, base, on* handlers, a url that is not https, assets/… or a #fragment) is cut out of the pasted text where it was written, every <style> block and linked stylesheet is folded into the css in document order, and the rest of the text is stored as it arrived. An https linked stylesheet is fetched by the host; one it cannot fetch is removed and reported, and so is one with a relative href, since a clipboard has no address to resolve it against. The document's <title> is the page's meta title. A data: image, named by an img's src or by a url() in a style attribute or a <style>, is stored through the host and its url replaced by assets/<file> where it was written. One that cannot be stored is reported: an img loses its src and keeps its alt, and a css url() is kept as written, as is a data: url in css that is not an image, which is reported too. No gates run on a paste; the console reports what the cleaning removed and folded, in ingest's sentences. A paste of more than 10,000 elements or four million characters is refused and lands nothing.
